reason: None of the cited evidence addresses the FeNiCrCoCu system, high-temperature sliding-induced dynamic recrystallization, or the role of deformation twins in wear. E1 discusses TiC reinforcement in a different HEA, E2 covers tensile strength of a refractory HEA, E3 describes load/speed effects on wear of HEA-reinforced copper, and E4 reports hardness/wear of various HEA coatings without the proposed mechanism. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Sliding at ~500 °C in FeNiCrCoCu coating induces dynamic recrystallization into an ultra-nanocrystalline, twinned tribolayer
This tribolayer homogenizes stress distribution and retards dislocation slip, reducing wear
Pre-existing nanocrystallinity and twins (from annealing) augment this shear-induced transformation
Annealed coating will show lower wear rates and fewer stress drop events than as-deposited coating
